candidate.answerReason: Each match eliminates one player. Exactly 99 of the 100 players are eliminated, so there are 99 matches, and 99 is divisible by 11.

methods.label: Count the eliminated players
methods.explanation:
Each match has exactly one loser, and that player is immediately eliminated. Thus no player can be the loser of two matches. Conversely, every player except the unbeaten champion must lose one match.

Pairing each match with its loser therefore counts every match exactly once. Since \(100-1=99\) players are eliminated, there are \(99\) matches. A bye eliminates nobody and does not affect this count.

Because \(99=9\cdot11\), the total is divisible by \(11\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses an elementary one-to-one pairing and whole-number arithmetic; formal function language is unnecessary.

candidate.annotationRationale: The tournament's one-match/one-elimination structure makes a one-to-one count the central target. Subtracting the champion from the total and recognizing a multiple of 11 are supporting arithmetic. The method explicitly establishes that no match or eliminated player is omitted or counted twice.
